A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same benchmarking framework. Their main text, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison despite renaming and page reflow.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original evaluations of 12 LLMs, and Section 3.7 and Appendix B report human verification of generated benchmark samples.

after.justification: The original LLM evaluations and human verification results are retained. Appendix B additionally reports inter-annotator agreement in Table 9.

M1.justification: The temporal knowledge checks, supporting-document retrieval, question construction, hop chaining, distractors, and answer-option design are unchanged. Correcting the Messi example to identify his sports team clarifies the existing object-as-answer rule.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Wikidata/Wikipedia single-hop and multi-hop QA scenarios, including generation, multiple-choice, and distractor settings. Summarization and code generation are newly discussed but are not evaluated.

E2.justification: Tables 4 and 5 retain the same 12 evaluated LLMs, and Figures 4 and 5 retain their respective model sets. Newly cited benchmarking methods do not participate in added empirical comparisons.

E3.justification: The time windows, interval widths, sample counts, cutoff dates, evaluation metrics, and prompts are unchanged. Appendix B retains three annotators and 100 samples each for Single-Hop Gold and Multi-Hop Gold; the added agreement analysis uses this retained audit design.

E4.justification: Appendix B and new Table 9 add an analysis of whether annotators agree on context and answer accuracy. Existing temporal-contamination, distractor, and task-difficulty analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: V2 first reports Raw Agreement and Gwet’s AC1, explaining their selection for predominantly positive annotations. This adds statistical reliability reporting without a documented increase in annotators, samples, or experimental runs.

E6.justification: The existing numerical entries in Tables 1–8 are unchanged. New Table 9 reports raw agreement of 0.96–0.98 and Gwet’s AC1 of 0.97–0.99 across the context/answer and single-/multi-hop assessments.

T1.justification: The triplet, temporal-window, sample, and multi-hop-chain definitions are unchanged. Neither version provides formal theorems or proofs, and the added agreement analysis introduces no mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: strictly contamination-free evaluation through updated real-world knowledge and an automated benchmark-building workflow. The benchmark rename and additional supporting analysis do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 3 adds reasons for focusing on QA and difficulties extending the framework to summarization or code generation. Appendix B explains coefficient selection and interprets agreement. The limitations discussion shortens the source-error caveat and removes the proposed use of additional or more rigorous sources.

D1.justification: The disclosed code/data repository path changes from bobxwu/AntiLeak-Bench to bobxwu/AntiLeakBench alongside the rename. This updates the access address; Appendix A’s construction details and Appendix C’s prompts remain unchanged, with no documented implementation or availability change.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations on contamination and dynamic benchmarking, including Ni, Qian, and Srivastava, plus Gwet for agreement and several survey/topic-modeling references. The substantive positioning against existing benchmarks remains largely unchanged; FASTopic’s publication update represents the same cited work.

P1.justification: V2 renames the benchmark, adds an author visiting-work footnote, corrects the single-hop example, and makes localized wording and explanatory revisions. The section sequence and overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 9 and updates Figures 4–5 with explicit year labels, cutoff-date markers, explanatory captions, and adjusted ticks/legends. Table 5 moves from page 7 to page 8, with associated appendix reflow; the remaining displays retain their structure.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1’s accuracy-only human audit, v2 adds agreement evidence in Appendix B/Table 9. Cutoff markers in Figures 4–5 and the QA-scope explanation also make the paper easier to assess. Although the source-quality limitation is less detailed, these changes provide a modest net gain in validation reporting and clarity without changing the main method or results.
